scope: Step 1 purposive foundation, not exhaustive; no experiments or focus selection
reading_depth_definition: Selected relevant full-text methods/evaluation reading; not replication

scholarly_sources.citation: Kritzinger, W., Karner, M., Traar, G., Henjes, J., & Sihn, W. (2018). Digital Twin in manufacturing: A categorical literature review and classification. IFAC-PapersOnLine, 51(11), 1016-1022.
scholarly_sources.question: How can manufacturing literature be categorized by integration?
scholarly_sources.method: Categorical literature review; model/shadow/twin distinction.
scholarly_sources.data: Literature corpus; counts not checked in full text.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Classification, not an empirical system benchmark.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: An influential integration taxonomy distinguishes digital models, shadows and twins; the abstract reports less literature at its highest integration level.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Manufacturing-specific and historical; not a universal definition or evidence of present scarcity.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Publisher indexed abstract verified; direct page fetch returned 403. No full-text method claims.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Publisher metadata and abstract only
scholarly_sources.relevance: Vocabulary baseline, to be compared with T02/T03/T11.

scholarly_sources.citation: Jones, D., Snider, C., Nassehi, A., Yon, J., & Hicks, B. (2020). Characterising the Digital Twin: A systematic literature review. CIRP Journal of Manufacturing Science and Technology, 29, 36-52.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed systematic review; author accepted manuscript read
scholarly_sources.question: Which concepts and processes recur across twin descriptions?
scholarly_sources.method: Google Scholar first 500 results plus citation expansion; thematic analysis.
scholarly_sources.data: 92 retained publications; searches September-October 2018.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Theme mapping; no operational accuracy benchmark.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Separates entity, environment, state, measurement, realization and synchronization rate. Discusses one-way definitions despite original bidirectional framing.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Manufacturing-heavy corpus; search horizon predates recent urban/neural work.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Open CC BY accepted manuscript retained locally; corpus methodology described.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: section 2, sections 3.1.5-3.1.13; manuscript pp.4-7,11-17; Fig.5 visually inspected (PDF page14).
scholarly_sources.relevance: Specify what is measured, what changes and at what rate, rather than calling a renderer a twin.

scholarly_sources.citation: Glaessgen, E. H., & Stargel, D. S. (2012). The Digital Twin Paradigm for Future NASA and U.S. Air Force Vehicles. 53rd AIAA/ASME/ASCE/AHS/ASC Structures, Structural Dynamics and Materials Conference, AIAA 2012-1818.
scholarly_sources.question: How could asset-specific models improve future vehicle sustainment?
scholarly_sources.method: Conceptual synthesis of physical models, onboard sensing and lifecycle records.
scholarly_sources.data: Illustrative aerospace cases; no integrated-twin trial dataset.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Discusses conventional practice and future capabilities; not a controlled comparative trial.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Defines a probabilistic multiphysics, multiscale asset-specific simulation informed by sensor and fleet history.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Aspirational aerospace framing; projected reliability gains are not demonstrated results.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: NASA public PDF accessible; no runnable integrated implementation established.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Targeted full text: Concept and Attributes, pp.6-10; introduction and summary.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Shows why the physical/data relationship and prediction matter beyond visualization.

scholarly_sources.citation: Kapteyn, M. G., Pretorius, J. V. R., & Willcox, K. E. (2021). A probabilistic graphical model foundation for enabling predictive digital twins at scale. Nature Computational Science, 1, 337-347.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed methods and experimental/simulation paper; author manuscript read
scholarly_sources.question: How can calibration, estimation, prediction and decisions share an uncertainty-aware formulation?
scholarly_sources.method: Probabilistic graphical model and Bayesian updating of a UAV structural model.
scholarly_sources.data: Physical wing geometry, load-displacement and dynamic response calibration; simulated operational mission and noisy strain observations.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Prior/posterior calibration; modal discrepancy; normalized strain prediction error; estimated versus prescribed structural-health evolution and control switching.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Demonstrates unified calibration and simulated health-aware operation; Fig.6 distinguishes estimation from future prediction and exposes unequal parameter uncertainty.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Operational demonstration is simulated, not validated fleet deployment; model discrepancy and observability remain challenges.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Paper reports public calibration and simulation repositories, but proprietary Akselos solver; model-output data supplied instead. Repositories not run.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: formulation, calibration/operational results pp.3-9, calibration methods pp.10-12, availability p.15; Fig.6 visually inspected.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Concrete example of uncertainty propagation and explicit held-future prediction, transferable as principles rather than highway results.

scholarly_sources.citation: Shao, G., Hightower, J., & Schindel, W. (2023). Credibility consideration for digital twins in manufacturing. Manufacturing Letters, 35, 24-28. Online December 2022.
scholarly_sources.question: What makes twin outputs credible for decisions?
scholarly_sources.method: Discusses verification, validation, uncertainty and extension of a twin framework standard.
scholarly_sources.data: Not established from accessible abstract.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: No numerical efficacy claim made from abstract.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: VVUQ belongs throughout the twin lifecycle; credibility also includes other factors.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Manufacturing scope; framework discussion is not empirical proof of a particular highway model.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: NIST abstract and publication-year reconciliation verified; linked PDF fetch failed.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Institutional abstract and citation metadata only
scholarly_sources.relevance: Separate software correctness, real-world agreement and uncertainty.

scholarly_sources.citation: Dembski, F., Wössner, U., Letzgus, M., Ruddat, M., & Yamu, C. (2020). Urban Digital Twins for Smart Cities and Citizens: The Case Study of Herrenberg, Germany. Sustainability, 12(6), 2307.
scholarly_sources.question: Can urban models and simulation support participatory planning?
scholarly_sources.method: Combines city geometry, space syntax, SUMO, OpenFOAM, sensors and COVISE/OpenCOVER immersive visualization.
scholarly_sources.data: Herrenberg city and environmental data; citizen observations; 39 survey respondents aged 16-80.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Nine-question survey, polarity profiles and open answers; Fig.8 compares prior-participation groups.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Demonstrates integrated urban visualization with broadly positive participant judgments.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Small nonrepresentative sample; no randomized interface comparator; positive opinions do not validate traffic or pollution prediction.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: CC BY publisher PDF retained; software named/public COVISE link, but end-to-end datasets and replay not established.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: section 3 components pp.4-8 and sections 4.3-5 pp.12-15; Fig.8 visually inspected (PDF page14).
scholarly_sources.relevance: Direct prior art for combining SUMO, urban models and immersive participation; integration alone is not a novelty claim.

scholarly_sources.citation: Ketzler, B., Naserentin, V., Latino, F., Zangelidis, C., Thuvander, L., & Logg, A. (2020). Digital Twins for Cities: A State of the Art Review. Built Environment, 46(4), 547-573.
scholarly_sources.question: How do urban twins relate to 3D city models?
scholarly_sources.method: Academic terminology review and practical examples from grey literature.
scholarly_sources.data: Literature; full corpus not checked.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Concept/application comparison, not an accuracy benchmark.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Urban usage extends beyond geometry to semantic, sensor and simulation information; no consensus definition reported.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Historical review and grey-literature examples do not independently validate deployment claims.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Institutional abstract/metadata accessible; full text not read.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Institutional abstract and bibliographic metadata
scholarly_sources.relevance: Broadens the foundation beyond traffic control.

scholarly_sources.citation: Slater, M., Banakou, D., Beacco, A., Gallego, J., Macia-Varela, F., & Oliva, R. (2022). A Separate Reality: An Update on Place Illusion and Plausibility in Virtual Reality. Frontiers in Virtual Reality, 3, 914392.
scholarly_sources.question: How should presence and plausibility be understood and measured?
scholarly_sources.method: Reviews competing constructs and measurement approaches.
scholarly_sources.data: Prior studies; no new single benchmark dataset.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Table 1 compares questionnaires, behavior/physiology, breaks, configuration transitions and sentiment methods.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Separates system affordances from subjective response and recommends triangulating measures.
scholarly_sources.limitations: A theoretical position with contested terminology; cited experiments were not all independently read.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Open full HTML; no new experiment to reproduce.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: Place Illusion and Plausibility, Coherence, Measurement and Table1; targeted full-text reading.
scholarly_sources.relevance: XR usefulness and perceived realism need task-specific measurement, separate from simulation validity.

scholarly_sources.citation: Latoschik, M. E., & Wienrich, C. (2022). Congruence and Plausibility, Not Presence: Pivotal Conditions for XR Experiences and Effects, a Novel Approach. Frontiers in Virtual Reality, 3, 694433.
scholarly_sources.question: Can a framework cover VR, AR and MR more broadly than place illusion?
scholarly_sources.method: Conceptual critique and proposed congruence/plausibility model.
scholarly_sources.data: No new experiment in this perspective.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Theoretical comparison rather than benchmark.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Offers a competing account of XR experience, explicitly challenging presence-centered framing.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Proposal is not established superiority; terminology differs from T08.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Open full HTML.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Targeted introduction and discussion of current presence-oriented theories
scholarly_sources.relevance: Avoid treating one XR taxonomy as universally accepted.

scholarly_sources.citation: Hofer, M., Hartmann, T., Eden, A., Ratan, R., & Hahn, L. (2020). The Role of Plausibility in the Experience of Spatial Presence in Virtual Environments. Frontiers in Virtual Reality, 1, 2.
scholarly_sources.question: Do external plausibility violations reduce spatial presence?
scholarly_sources.method: Randomized 2x2x2 between-subject design: plausibility, HMD/monitor immersion, cognitive load.
scholarly_sources.data: 195 undergraduates exploring a virtual house.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: SPES self-location/possible-action scales; ANOVA and one-tailed equivalence tests using delta=0.15.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: HMD condition increased presence; plausibility manipulation changed perceived plausibility but did not reduce presence under tested conditions.
scholarly_sources.limitations: House exploration/student sample; one kind of inconsistency; possible-actions residual normality issue; no highway decision or transfer measure.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Open HTML methods; no independently verified runnable artifact.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: Current Study, Method, Measures, Results and Discussion full sections.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Empirical warning against using subjective presence as a proxy for physical realism or predictive truth.

scholarly_sources.citation: Grübel, J., Thrash, T., Aguilar, L., Gath-Morad, M., Chatain, J., Sumner, R. W., Hölscher, C., & Schinazi, V. R. (2022). The Hitchhiker's Guide to Fused Twins: A Review of Access to Digital Twins in situ in Smart Cities. Remote Sensing, 14(13), 3095.
scholarly_sources.type: Review with journal DOI; author-deposited preprint abstract accessed
scholarly_sources.question: How can situated analytics connect urban data to its physical location?
scholarly_sources.method: Reviews twins, situated analytics and smart cities; proposes fused-twin framing.
scholarly_sources.data: Literature/examples; detailed corpus not checked.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: No new comparative effect size established by accessed abstract.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Connects physical, data, analytical, virtual and connection environments to in-situ access.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Conceptual potential is not evidence that AR improves every decision; full methods not read.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: arXiv v2 dated 2022-06-08; publisher fetch failed.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Author abstract/version metadata only
scholarly_sources.relevance: XR as spatially situated access, beyond a desktop or immersive replica.

scholarly_sources.citation: Lei, B., Janssen, P., Stoter, J., & Biljecki, F. (2023). Challenges of urban digital twins: A systematic review and a Delphi expert survey. Automation in Construction, 147, 104716.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed systematic review and expert survey
scholarly_sources.question: Which technical and nontechnical obstacles affect urban twins?
scholarly_sources.method: Literature review plus three-round Delphi survey.
scholarly_sources.data: 34 reviewed papers; expert panel (count not independently checked here).
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Expert issue-severity ratings on five-point scale; synthesis mapped to lifecycle.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Combined taxonomy includes 14 technical and 9 nontechnical challenges; social/legal/practical-value concerns supplement data and interoperability problems.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Expert judgment and historical corpus; severity is not causal evidence or a ranking for this team.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Publisher indexed methods/results inspected; institutional metadata confirms citation; repository PDF fetch timed out.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Targeted publisher text: Delphi design, Results, Discussion, Conclusion; not counted as deep anchor
scholarly_sources.relevance: Scope, purpose, governance and data maintenance belong in feasibility, not only rendering technology.

scholarly_sources.citation: Mildenhall, Ben; Srinivasan, Pratul P.; Tancik, Matthew; Barron, Jonathan T.; Ramamoorthi, Ravi; Ng, Ren (2020). NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis. ECCV.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; author manuscript read
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep selected full text: Sections 3-6.4 and conclusion; PDF pp. 7-10, 13-14; Table 1 p.10 visually inspected.
scholarly_sources.question: Can a continuous learned volume synthesize unseen views?
scholarly_sources.method: Scene-specific density and directional-color MLP, differentiable volume rendering, positional encoding and hierarchical sampling.
scholarly_sources.data: Synthetic objects and eight real forward-facing scenes.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS against SRN, Neural Volumes and LLFF; component ablations.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Static posed-image setting; expensive original optimization; photometric scores do not validate metric road geometry.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Foundational implicit appearance representation; separate rendering accuracy from physical validity.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Strong view synthesis; not uniformly best: real forward-facing LPIPS is 0.250 versus LLFF 0.212.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Public manuscript and implementation linked by authors; no reproduction performed.

scholarly_sources.citation: Kerbl, Bernhard; Kopanas, Georgios; Leimkühler, Thomas; Drettakis, George (2023). 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering. ACM Transactions on Graphics 42(4).
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep selected full text: Sections 3-7.4, Table 1; PDF p.7 Figure 5 visually inspected.
scholarly_sources.question: Can scene fitting retain image quality while rendering interactively?
scholarly_sources.method: Optimize explicit anisotropic Gaussians from SfM initialization; density control and tile-based differentiable rasterization.
scholarly_sources.data: Mip-NeRF360, Tanks and Temples, Deep Blending; synthetic scenes.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, training time, FPS and memory versus Mip-NeRF360, InstantNGP and Plenoxels.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Static scenes; poorly observed regions, popping and memory cost. No automatic watertight collider guarantee.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Interactive XR appearance; requires separate geometry validation.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: 30K Mip-NeRF360 result: 134 FPS and PSNR 27.21; comparator Mip-NeRF360 PSNR 27.69. Speed and quality are separate tradeoffs.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Public implementation linked by paper; benchmark figures are reported results, not local measurements.

scholarly_sources.citation: Wang, Shuzhe; Leroy, Vincent; Cabon, Yohann; Chidlovskii, Boris; Revaud, Jerome (2024). DUSt3R: Geometric 3D Vision Made Easy. CVPR, 20697-20709.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; revised author manuscript
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep selected full text: Section 3 method, Section 4 evaluation; PDF pp.7-8 visually checked. HTML subsection numbering differs from PDF.
scholarly_sources.question: Can images yield dense geometry without supplied camera calibration?
scholarly_sources.method: Transformer predicts paired pointmaps and confidences; multi-pair global alignment.
scholarly_sources.data: Mixed indoor/outdoor training; evaluation includes 7Scenes, Cambridge, CO3Dv2, RealEstate10K and depth benchmarks.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Pose errors, relative pose accuracy, depth relative error/inlier ratio; compares HLoc, pose methods and MVS methods under distinct input assumptions.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Multi-view depth predictions are scale ambiguous and median-aligned to ground truth. Confidence is not verified calibrated uncertainty; highway accuracy untested here.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Geometry from sparse imagery, with external georeferencing and scale evidence still required.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Unifies several geometric tasks; evaluation must distinguish supplied poses and scale alignment.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Public code/models: https://github.com/naver/dust3r ; licenses require separate checking.

scholarly_sources.citation: Schönberger, Johannes L.; Frahm, Jan-Michael (2016). Structure-from-Motion Revisited. CVPR, 4104-4113.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Publisher abstract/metadata only; full PDF not deeply read.
scholarly_sources.question: How can incremental SfM improve general reconstruction?
scholarly_sources.method: Incremental SfM pipeline; detailed modules not extracted in this edition.
scholarly_sources.data: Not extracted.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Not extracted; no quantitative claim adopted.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Abstract cannot substantiate benchmark superiority; original algorithm distinct from current COLMAP releases.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Classical camera/point reconstruction baseline and prerequisite for many radiance-field workflows.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Provides an open reconstruction pipeline addressing robustness, accuracy, completeness and scalability.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Public implementation reported by publisher; version must be pinned for experiments.

scholarly_sources.citation: Campos, Carlos; Elvira, Richard; Gómez Rodríguez, Juan J.; Montiel, José M. M.; Tardós, Juan D. (2021). ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial, and Multimap SLAM. IEEE Transactions on Robotics 37(6), 1874-1890.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Abstract, metadata and official repository checked; no full-method extraction.
scholarly_sources.question: How can visual/inertial SLAM reuse multiple maps?
scholarly_sources.method: Feature-based visual/inertial estimation with map merging; abstract-level description.
scholarly_sources.data: EuRoC and TUM-VI named in abstract/repository.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Detailed baseline protocol not read; no numeric accuracy adopted.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Published indoor/drone evidence is not a Los Angeles highway robustness guarantee.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Separates motion tracking and mapping from rendered appearance.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Public system supports monocular, stereo and RGB-D configurations, including inertial variants.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: https://github.com/UZ-SLAMLab/ORB_SLAM3 ; public examples and GPLv3 license.

scholarly_sources.citation: Brachmann, Eric; Cavallari, Tommaso; Prisacariu, Victor Adrian (2023). Accelerated Coordinate Encoding: Learning to Relocalize in Minutes using RGB and Poses. CVPR.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; author project page
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Author page method/results/dataset sections; full paper not read.
scholarly_sources.question: Can scene-coordinate relocalization mapping become faster?
scholarly_sources.method: Fixed feature backbone, scene-specific MLP, mixed-view feature batches and reprojection training; pose via RANSAC/PnP.
scholarly_sources.data: 7Scenes, 12Scenes, Cambridge and Wayspots illustrated; Wayspots has ten outdoor scenes.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Author reports comparison with DSAC*; complete benchmark protocol not extracted.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Larger scenes may need ensembles; Wayspots reference poses use SfM; not universal metric ground truth.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Research behind historical Niantic relocalization; cannot identify current VPS backend solely from this paper.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Reports five-minute scene mapping and 4 MB weights in its setup.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Code/data linked on author page.

scholarly_sources.citation: Numan, Nels; Brostow, Gabriel; Park, Suhyun; Julier, Simon; Steed, Anthony; Van Brummelen, Jessica (2025). CoCreatAR: Enhancing Authoring of Outdoor Augmented Reality Experiences Through Asymmetric Collaboration. CHI.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; author project page
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Author page abstract, system and results overview; full paper not read.
scholarly_sources.question: Can on-site/remote collaboration improve outdoor AR authoring?
scholarly_sources.method: Synchronous asymmetric system sharing captures, annotations and context.
scholarly_sources.data: Formative n=25 and exploratory n=32 studies reported.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Asynchronous-workflow comparator; engagement, confidence and task-load discussion. Instruments/statistical analysis not extracted.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Not evidence of highway inspection or traffic-safety improvement.
scholarly_sources.relevance: XR can be evaluated as a human workflow, beyond rendering frame rate.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Authors report engagement/confidence benefits; task-load evidence described as preliminary.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: System overview public; code availability not verified.

scholarly_sources.citation: Turkulainen, Matias; Krishnan, Akshay; Aleotti, Filippo; Sayed, Mohamed; Garcia-Hernando, Guillermo; Kannala, Juho; Solin, Arno; Brostow, Gabriel; Turmukhambetov, Daniyar (2026). Cross-View Splatter: Feed-Forward View Synthesis with Georeferenced Images. CVPR, 40959-40970.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; CVF proceedings verified
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Author project page method and result table; full paper not read.
scholarly_sources.question: Can overhead imagery improve sparse ground-view synthesis?
scholarly_sources.method: VGGT-based feed-forward Gaussians combine GPS-tagged ground photos and orthorectified imagery.
scholarly_sources.data: Geolocalized ten Tanks and Temples and forty DL3DV scenes.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Two-context-view PSNR/LPIPS versus MVSplat, DepthSplat, NoPoSplat, Long-LRM, AnySplat.
scholarly_sources.limitations: No highway geometry/behavior validation established; author page says some release materials forthcoming.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Close prior work for aerial-ground fusion, so combining these modalities alone is not a novelty argument.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Higher PSNR but worse LPIPS than AnySplat in displayed table; broad superiority would overstate evidence.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Code/data link present; actual artifact completeness not verified.

scholarly_sources.citation: Tirado-Garín, Javier; Paul, Alan Savio; Chen, Shuai; Barroso-Laguna, Axel; Cavallari, Tommaso; Turmukhambetov, Daniyar; Prisacariu, Victor Adrian; Brachmann, Eric (2026). AutoCompass: Accurate Visual Localization on Public Maps by Learning from Weak Labels. ECCV; official accepted-paper listing verified.
scholarly_sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference research; ECCV acceptance verified
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Author page methods and evaluation labels; full paper not read.
scholarly_sources.question: Can map matching learn from noisy georeferencing?
scholarly_sources.method: GPS tolerance regions and optional relative-pose supervision for neural map matching.
scholarly_sources.data: KITTI, Oxford Day-and-Night and LaMAria.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Recall at one-meter thresholds; OrienterNet and GPS comparisons described; numerical plots not extracted.
scholarly_sources.limitations: No full protocol/statistical audit; three-DoF map matching is not six-DoF surveyed registration.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Geospatial labels themselves may be uncertain.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Authors report improved localization with weak labels.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Project page public; complete code/model release not verified.

scholarly_sources.citation: Lague, D., Brodu, N., & Leroux, J. (2013). Accurate 3D comparison of complex topography with terrestrial laser scanner: application to the Rangitikei canyon (N-Z). ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, 82, 10–26.
scholarly_sources.type: peer-reviewed methods and field study; author manuscript read
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Deep selected sections: 2.4, 3.1–3.4, 4.1–4.2, 5.2–5.3; author PDF pages 5–12 and 17–20. Figures 3 and 8 visually inspected locally (PDF pages 7 and 18). Not replicated.
scholarly_sources.question: How can two rough 3D surfaces be compared with local change uncertainty?
scholarly_sources.method: M3C2 projects local point sets along estimated surface normals and estimates confidence bounds.
scholarly_sources.data: Synthetic shifted noisy planes and repeat terrestrial scans of Rangitikei canyon.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Compares nearest-neighbor C2C, height-function C2C and cloud-to-mesh; examines displacement error and no-change rejection under resampling.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Local averaging and uncertainty estimates improve interpretable change measurement in evaluated settings.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Registration assumptions, roughness, density and scale affect confidence calibration; Figure 8 shows failure at some scales. Canyon precision is not a highway accuracy guarantee.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Separate actual change from sampling/registration differences.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Public author manuscript; CloudCompare implementation described; no local reproduction or data-license audit.

scholarly_sources.citation: Biljecki, F., Stoter, J., Ledoux, H., Zlatanova, S., & Çöltekin, A. (2015). Applications of 3D City Models: State of the Art Review. ISPRS International Journal of Geo-Information, 4(4), 2842–2889.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Selected full-text sections 2, 3.1–3.4 and 5; not all application subsections read.
scholarly_sources.question: What do people use 3D city models for?
scholarly_sources.method: Literature and project-document classification.
scholarly_sources.data: Scientific papers, reports and online resources.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Taxonomy of 29 use cases; no controlled benchmark or pooled effect size.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Urban 3D applications span visualization and analysis, beyond traffic.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Subjective category boundaries; reported application does not independently demonstrate benefit; historical coverage.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Keeps the foundation broader than vehicle control and separates popularity from utility.
scholarly_sources.reproducibility_access: Open full text and references; no re-screening performed.

scholarly_sources.citation: Kutzner, T., Chaturvedi, K., & Kolbe, T. H. (2020). CityGML 3.0: New Functions Open Up New Applications. PFG, 88, 43–61.
scholarly_sources.reading_depth: Selected full-text sections 1–2, 4 (Dynamizers), 5.1–5.2, 6.1–6.4, 7 through publisher HTML. Repository PDF download returned HTML and was removed; no local PDF claim.
scholarly_sources.question: How should semantic urban objects support geometry, time and applications?
scholarly_sources.method: Modular conceptual model and illustrative conversions/use cases.
scholarly_sources.data: City/IFC examples including Berlin Moabit; not a highway sensor benchmark.
scholarly_sources.evaluation: Schema and implementation examples; no predictive-accuracy comparison.
scholarly_sources.supported_finding: Transportation spaces, time-varying property links and point-cloud representation can be explicitly modeled.
scholarly_sources.limitations: Describes then-proposed standard; current normative specifications must govern implementations. Expressiveness does not establish complete data or software support.
scholarly_sources.relevance: Geometry and semantics need a declared mapping, even if the viewer uses USD.
